5.8 Proposed Future Testing Plan 
The future testing plan for the proposed e-learning application aims to evaluate 
the long-term viability and effectiveness on student engagement, retention, and 
academic performance. Like with the short-term study was conducted within this 
document, this investigation will primarily focus on the applications with a multi-
faceted feature set designed around gamification and short-form content, which 
are hypothesised to significantly enhance learning outcomes. 
To gage the effectiveness of each of these features, the testing plan will be 
comprised of multiple research methodologies, including A/B testing, a 
longitudinal study, and qualitative feedback via interviews and surveys. 
A/B testing will serve as the bedrock for this investigation. Utilising this strategy 
two versions of the application will be released; version alpha will, include 
features such as spaced-repetition, short-form content, and gamified features, 
while the beta group will have a selection of these features removed. Each group 
will be assigned versions of the application at random, and possibly at different 
times to help further validate hypotheses.  
The metrics used within this study will include session duration, frequency of 
application usage, exam scores, and retention rates. These attributes will act as 
a guide to gage which features are most effective at enhancing engagement and 
bolstering academic performance. 
To accompany the A/B testing, a longitudinal study will track a GCSE group of 
students using the application over the course of an academic year. An extended 
observational study will allow for an analysis of the applications effects overtime, 
looking into how sustained usage may affect final exam results. Academic 
performance will be measured at set intervals, notably at the beginning of the 
year, before the Christmas and easter break, and finally at the end of the year.
